teacher_issue: Area decrease plus Bernoulli pressure
scientific_teacher_note: For steady incompressible leak-free one-streamline water, continuity increases velocity in the smaller area. To conclude lower static pressure from basic Bernoulli, neglect viscous head loss and shaft work and compare equal elevations; stem calls only pipe smooth and flow steady, not explicitly ideal. Source D is intended, but needs a teacher-approved model qualifier.

teacher_issue: Same-speed vertical rise
scientific_teacher_note: At unchanged speed and constant water density in one ideal streamline, P2=P1−rho*g*4 m; upper static pressure is lower. Original B valid under stated ideal conditions.

teacher_issue: Same-speed vertical descent
scientific_teacher_note: At equal speed and lower elevation, less gravitational energy per volume is balanced by higher static pressure; original B within the ideal same-streamline model.

teacher_issue: Rising and narrowing jointly reduce pressure
scientific_teacher_note: Steady incompressible flow in an unbranched rising and narrowing ideal pipe means both increased kinetic density and increased elevation consume pressure energy; original A. Avoid assuming an arbitrary external pump.

teacher_issue: Descending widening pipe
scientific_teacher_note: At steady no-leak incompressible ideal flow, both decreased speed and lower elevation raise the static-pressure term, supporting original B.

teacher_issue: Two gauges with different section areas
scientific_teacher_note: For the same ideal horizontal unbranched flow, smaller section implies higher mean speed and lower static pressure. Original C; gauges measure static rather than stagnation pressure.

teacher_issue: Same tube area does not alone fix speed when unsteady
scientific_teacher_note: The source says water rises in an unchanged-area tube but does not explicitly specify steady incompressible flow without leaks. A=constant gives equal section speeds from Q=Av only if steady discharge is conserved; then kinetic term stays unchanged and rho*g*h rises, giving original C conditionally. Clarify model before an individually approved final-paper item.

teacher_issue: Friction requires nonideal head-loss balance
scientific_teacher_note: Substantial friction dissipates mechanical energy, invalidating basic lossless Bernoulli equality; source D. This also relates to summative B41 real-fluid viscosity, but an explanation of failure is not automatically a complete B40 Application item. Source physics verified.

teacher_issue: Equal displaced volumes derive from continuity
scientific_teacher_note: For steady incompressible no-leak one-inlet/outlet fluid, A1*v1*dt=A2*v2*dt, so answer B. The isolated item tests continuity/conservation of mass rather than independent application of Bernoulli pressure-height-speed B40; candidate B36 only until teacher review.

teacher_issue: Pressure-work sign convention
scientific_teacher_note: Given W1=+P1*V and W2=−P2*V on the selected moving fluid element, Wnet=(P1−P2)*V (D). This is directly supported by original printed NBF p99–100 derivation but is supporting algebra rather than entire Bernoulli pressure/speed/height application.

teacher_issue: Pump adds energy omitted by unmodified Bernoulli
scientific_teacher_note: A pump between stations adds shaft work requiring an extended energy equation. Original B is correct, but the textbook's basic Bernoulli equation p99–100 has no pump-head term, so classify as a boundary-of-model conceptual item and do not claim exact original formula or automatic individual summative B40 Application eligibility.

teacher_issue: Slowing at equal elevation raises pressure
scientific_teacher_note: Along an ideal same-height streamline, reducing speed from 8 to 4 m/s lowers kinetic-energy density and raises static pressure. Original C; water density not required for this qualitative direction.

teacher_issue: Wider and higher sections have competing pressure effects
scientific_teacher_note: A rise increases rho*g*h and tends to lower P while widening decreases speed at fixed discharge and tends to raise P. Which wins depends on areas, speeds and elevation change (B), but require an ideal steady incompressible lossless same-streamline model to infer these as the only effects; stem does not explicitly state them.

teacher_issue: Seven-metre height term
scientific_teacher_note: Comparing 1 m and 8 m means a rho*g*(7 m) difference when density is constant; neglecting elevation is wrong, source D. How numerically important it is depends on the other energy terms.

teacher_issue: Equal speed and elevation means equal static pressure
scientific_teacher_note: On the same ideal streamline with common Bernoulli constant, equal v and h imply equal P; original C. This is not a universal comparison across unrelated streams.

teacher_issue: Density change is a comparison of separate calculations
scientific_teacher_note: At fixed chosen v1,v2, delta P=0.5*rho*(v2²−v1²) and changing rho from 1000 to 800 multiplies the pressure difference by 0.8, so original A. Interpret as two hypothetical constant-density fluids/conditions rather than one incompressible fluid changing its density along its streamline.

teacher_issue: Bernoulli horizontal pressure drop from 4 to 8 m/s
scientific_teacher_note: For rho_water≈1000 kg/m³, ΔP=0.5*1000*(8²−4²)=24000 Pa=24 kPa, source C. Density is implicit in stem, so identify assumed conventional value.

teacher_issue: Same cross-section does not guarantee equal speed in compressible flow
scientific_teacher_note: The item says 'a fluid' moves steadily with identical areas and no losses/pumps but does not explicitly require incompressibility or identical densities. For a compressible steady stream, rho*A*v constant can allow different speeds at equal A, and pressures may differ. Source C is valid only for constant-density steady flow along one ideal streamline; fix wording before exam certification.

teacher_issue: Pressure work energizes rising accelerating fluid
scientific_teacher_note: An ideal fluid parcel's gains in KE and gravitational PE can come from net pressure work, original D. This is qualitative energy-transfer reasoning and not automatically a full Application-level two-section numerical problem.

teacher_issue: Recognition of constant Bernoulli sum versus full application
scientific_teacher_note: Source A states P+0.5*rho*v²+rho*g*h is constant along the same ideal streamline. It is an accurate formula-concept item but original teacher tag is Understanding, not individually an official Summative/Application B40 examination item.
